purpose: Test a fixed-size token pool that can retain parts of more prior frames, using Lean usage and early foreground/background contrast with matched controls.
scope: Experimental forward-only single-object CPU FP32 inference on the existing isolated raw-history Lean token-window worktree, no new trained attention. The 16,384 represented-spatial-feature budget includes a fixed 3,072 insurance reserve and protects the full 4,096-token conditioning and newest grids. At most 5,120 compressed older tokens share the remaining space. Position tensors, pointers, anchors, masks, score metadata and transient allocations are separately reported and are outside that feature-token budget.
scores: For each source memory, before author's pending compression, retain the author's selected 1,024 token IDs in their original order. Store tied empirical percentile ranks of the author's first-read usage on its complete 4,096 grid, frozen before cross-frame pooling; derive per-grid foreground-minus-background cosine contrast from the existing early-FPN prototype code, using only the original automatic prompt mask. Compute pooled early score on the source frame, align via original 64x64 spatial coordinates, and retain matching metadata with features and positions. Initial prototype failure is a fail-closed unsupported case, not an adaptive detector or confidence gate.
arms: At every write, select exactly min(5120, eligible tokens) across all resident older sources. Usage ranks alone; fixed balanced contrast ranking (half of the capacity favors usage plus foreground contrast and half favors usage plus background contrast, without hard foreground labels); or deterministic round-robin across frames with bit-reversed spatial ordering. Same author preselection, protected memories, cost budget, processing schedule, model weights and inputs. Dropped tokens cannot be recovered; older surviving token groups can span more frames than the previous whole-entry window. No new redetection, confidence gate, label input, or inference threshold.
validation: Two independent score-observer-only seq3 replays must reproduce the existing raw-window seq3 masks, positions, selection and author events exactly. Each pool strategy must have two repeatable label-free seq3 runs that preserve prompt and early causal prefix, paired feature/position/grid IDs, valid author-selection metadata, exact reserved budgets at each write, pointer-count traces and model integrity. The distributed control must demonstrate retention spanning more source frames than the baseline when the sequence is long enough. Independently rehash and verify all gates before selected-video inference; score metadata and transient bytes are not free and must be reported.
limitations: Usage percentiles are relative to each source's first read and are not proven causal utilities or fully comparable across time. Balanced signed contrast is not a trained channel-attention module and does not reproduce CMSA CMA. Incorrect initial prompts can contaminate prototypes; fixed role allocation may discard useful boundary tokens. Frame times beyond learned slots reuse the oldest available slot. Experiments are on previously inspected sequences, and initial sample allocation and normalization are hypotheses.
